# Frontend Design

Use this skill when you need to create or refine a premium frontend UI for a web app, landing page, dashboard, or portfolio.

## Goals
- Keep the interface modern, responsive, and conversion-friendly.
- Use strong visual hierarchy, spacing, contrast, and typography.
- Prefer semantic HTML, accessible labels, and keyboard-friendly interactions.
- Balance aesthetics with performance and maintainability.

## Default approach
- Start with a clean layout and clear content hierarchy.
- Choose a restrained color palette with one accent system and consistent spacing rules.
- Prefer reusable components and CSS variables over ad-hoc styling.
- Use subtle gradients, soft borders, and motion only when they clarify use and improve polish.
- Validate on mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints before wrapping up.

## Examples
- Good: a hero section with strong headline, CTA hierarchy, trust badges, and responsive layout.
- Good: a card grid with consistent spacing, readable text, and accessible contrast.
- Avoid: overloading a page with too many colors, competing CTAs, or tiny text.

## Quality bar
- No broken layout at common viewport sizes.
- Buttons and links must be obvious and touch-friendly.
- Content should feel premium but still be fast and easy to scan.
- Code should stay clean and easy for future iterations.
